newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Desc Q1 op earnings seen strong.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Desc Q1 op earnings seen strong.

text.p: Mexican industrial conglomerate Desc Sociedad Industrial de Fomento S.A de C.V. is expected to report strong first quarter operating earnings fueled by its autoparts division, analysts said.

"We expect a good (11 percent) increase in sales year-on-year driven by the recent acquisition of Borg-Warner's (Automotive Inc) transmission business," analyst Kerry McHugh of Goldman Sachs in New York wrote in a recent report.

Borg-Warner Automotive Inc sold a transmission plant in October 1996 located in Muncie, Indiana to Transmisiones y Equipos Mecanicos S.A. de C.V., a joint venture between Desc and Toledo, Ohio-based Dana Corp.
A survey of four analysts predicted average net earnings per share of 1.41 pesos for the first quarter in 1997, compared with 2.14 pesos posted for the same quarter last year.
Nonetheless, analysts all stressed that non-cash items, such as foreign exchange gains and monetary earnings, distorted the net earnings figures and predicted stronger operating earnings for Desc.
"The reason they have less monetary gains is that they have less debt and more cash, which is positive," said Shayne McGuire of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Mexico City.

McGuire estimated that earnings per share, after subtracting foreign exchange and monetary gains, would rise to 0.90 pesos for the first quarter in 1997, up from a year-ago figure of 0.63 pesos, a real increase of 14 percent.

"Desc should report stronger operating earnings because they have less dollar-denominated debt, the peso is relatively stronger and the domestic market is picking up," said Daniel Goldstein, of ING Barings in Mexico City.

"It should be a good report with no great surprises," said Robert Hulme of Interacciones in New York. "Autoparts will be flat, with a downturn in the U.S. market offset by a rise in domestic consumption."
The analysts said margins in Desc's chemicals division would suffer from lower world prices, but this would not lead to a lower market share or competitive disadvantages.
Regarding the smaller agribusiness and real estate divisions, McHugh said "higher operating margins in in agribusiness will likely make up for any shortfall in real estate profits."
Desc is expected to post first quarter earnings on April 24.
